chapter: After the music: Army, public service, family
title: Quitting music for the public service and working the racetrack
summary: He quit playing around 1923 for 41 years with the public service, retired about 1964, and now works as a mutuel auditor at the fairgrounds.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: what about uh what have you done since you quit playing music well I worked for the public service

and went to work for public service I was 41 years there 41 years with the north public service and I retired there about six years ago so I spent practically half my life with with the public service
Yes, I was there 41 years. So 47 years ago you quit playing music? Yeah. Oh, Lord, I need my pencil to figure that out. This is 1970, I do believe. Yeah. So it was about 1923 you quit playing music?
It had to be, yeah. Somewhere around there, because I'll say I quit playing and I just went to the public service in those days. 41 years there. And I'm about six years away from there now.
And you've been working days at all since then?
No, I generally work at the fairgrounds and the Jefferson Trot when they open.
That's all I do. Do you work behind a window or something?
Behind the door, behind these boys, they work in the windows. I didn't like that window stuff.
Handing up money. I didn't care too much about that. I've seen too many of them losing money, you know, to work all day for nothing.
